title: Chicken Caesar Wraps
shortDescription: Grilled chicken, romaine, and Parmesan in flour tortillas
subtitle: Grilled chicken, romaine, and Parmesan in flour tortillas
description: Chicken breasts are seasoned and grilled, then sliced and rolled with chopped romaine, Caesar dressing, and Parmesan in large flour tortillas. Cut on a bias so cross-sections show chicken, greens, and dressing — not a mystery burrito.

steps.title: Marinate chicken and prep the wrap line
steps.instruction: Pound chicken to even thickness. Toss with olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Chop romaine and grate Parmesan. Set dressing and tortillas on the line — for 14 firefighters, plan 12–14 wraps across two trays.

steps.title: Grill the chicken
steps.instruction: Heat grill or grill pan over medium-high. Grill chicken 5–7 minutes per side until 160°F, then rest 5 minutes and slice into strips. Chicken should show grill marks — that is what sells this as Caesar wraps, not cold deli meat.

steps.title: Build the filling
steps.instruction: Toss romaine with enough dressing to coat lightly — not swimming. Fold in half the Parmesan. Taste for salt and acid; Caesar should be bold before it goes in the tortilla.

steps.title: Roll the wraps
steps.instruction: Warm tortillas 20 seconds per side on the grill or in a dry skillet. Layer chicken, dressed romaine, and remaining Parmesan across the centre. Fold sides in and roll tight. Cut on a bias for service so grilled chicken, romaine, and dressing show in cross-section.

steps.title: Hold and serve
steps.instruction: Wrap each in foil and hold at 200°F up to 20 minutes if calls interrupt. Serve with lemon wedges and extra Parmesan at the line. Do not stack unwrapped wraps — they steam and tear.

proTips: A light smear of dressing on the tortilla before filling helps every bite taste like Caesar.
If romaine wilts, use hearts only and keep chilled until the last minute.
Substitute grilled chicken thighs if breasts dry out on your grill — pull at 175°F.
tonightSpread: Simple tomato soup cups for dunking if you have kettle on
leftovers: Chop wraps into a chopped salad for next-day lunch
Slice chicken for a green salad
whyCrewsLikeIt: Caesar is familiar; wraps travel better than salad bowls in the truck. Grilled chicken reads as a real meal, not deli meat, and the line can hold wrapped bundles in foil at 200°F.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate chicken up to 4 hours. Wash and dry romaine early — wet greens sog out tortillas. Roll tight, tuck ends, and wrap each in foil. Hold up to 20 minutes in a warm oven; slice just before serving for best cross-section photos and eating.
